# FAS

Evidence-first security analysis for AI agents and modern software. FAS correlates observations into provenance-aware evidence, attack paths, exploitability analysis, formal verdicts, and remediation verification.

## Core documentation

- [README](README.md): product overview, quick start, capabilities, boundaries, configuration summary.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): documentation architecture and canonical sources.
- [Tutorials](docs/tutorials/README.md): first-run learning paths.
- [How-to guides](docs/how-to/README.md): task-oriented procedures.
- [Explanation](docs/explanation/README.md): evidence-first semantics and authority boundaries.
- [Reference](docs/reference/README.md): CLI, configuration, environment variables, and contracts.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md): system structure and invariants.
- [Evidence Model](docs/evidence-model/README.md): observation/evidence/provenance semantics.
- [Threat Model](docs/threat-model/README.md): trust boundaries and threats.
- [ADRs](docs/decisions/README.md): recorded architectural and security decisions.
- [Security Policy](SECURITY.md): vulnerability reporting and runtime security boundaries.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): development and contribution rules.

## Important concepts

- Observation is not evidence.
- Evidence is not automatically a finding.
- A finding is not automatically a proven vulnerability.
- LLM output is advisory and never authoritative evidence.
- Missing evidence remains explicit.
- Remediation requires scoped before/after verification.
- FAS is complementary to deterministic security scanners.

- Source: [src/fas](src/fas/)

- FAS-Bench: https://github.com/LloydCoder/fas-bench

## Constraints

Do not describe FAS as providing universal vulnerability coverage, complete attack-path enumeration, arbitrary candidate-repository execution, formal standards compliance, or a guarantee that a verdict means the entire analyzed system is secure.
